Minutes of the Monetary Policy Board Meeting

Sydney – 15 and 16 June 2026

Members present

Michele Bullock (Governor and Chair), Andrew Hauser (Deputy Governor and Deputy Chair), Marnie Baker AM, Renée Fry-McKibbin, Ian Harper AO.

Others present

Sarah Hunter (Assistant Governor, Economic), Anthony Dickman (Secretary).

Financial conditions

Members observed that financial conditions had eased modestly since the previous meeting, and that credit spreads had narrowed. The Australian dollar had depreciated a little, in line with a decline in yield differentials.

Economic conditions

Members discussed the March quarter national accounts. Members noted that GDP had increased by 0.9 per cent in the second quarter of 2026. Members noted that the unemployment rate declined to 4.1 per cent in the first quarter of 2026. Members observed that wage growth remained elevated.

Considerations for monetary policy

Members judged that the stance of monetary policy remained appropriate. The Board agreed that future decisions would depend on the incoming data. Some members assessed that the risks to the outlook were broadly balanced. A majority of the Board judged that the risks to inflation were to the upside. One member noted that the risks to growth had tilted to the downside. Members noted that inflation had increased to 2.4 per cent in the second quarter of 2026. Members noted that inflation expectations remained well anchored.

The decision

The Board decided unanimously to leave the cash rate target unchanged at 4.35 per cent.

Framework for additional monetary policy tools

Following the in-principle approval at the previous meeting, the Board approved the framework for additional monetary policy tools.
